title: Co-immunoprecipitation and semi-quantitative immunoblotting for the analysis of protein-protein interactions
protocol: Aspirate the cell culture medium.
Add 5 mL of sterile PBS to wash the cells.
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 1 mL trypsin/EDTA solution.
Incubate at 37°C in the cell culture incubator for around 2 min or until the cells detach.
Add 8 mL of PBS and resuspend the cells.
Collect the cell suspension in a 50 mL conical tube.
Spin down the cells at 180 × g for 2 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 5–10 mL PBS.
Mix 20 μL cell suspension with 20 μL trypan blue solution in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Pipette the mixture into a cell counting slide.
Count live cells manually with a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter to determine the cell density.
Exclude trypan blue stained dead cells from the count.
Calculate the required volume of cell suspension per 10 cm dish, needing 5 × 10^6 cells.
Prepare cell master mix by filling 10 mL of DMEM/10% FBS/AA medium in a 50 mL conical tube.
Add the corresponding calculated volume of cell suspension to the conical tube.
Mix thoroughly by inverting the tube.
Add 10 mL of cell master mix per 10 cm dish.
Place the dishes in the incubator for 7–8 hours.
Thaw a fresh aliquot of PEI transfection solution when needed.
Prepare the transfection mix using DMEM medium without serum or antibiotics.
Add DMEM to two microcentrifuge tubes.
Add plasmid DNA to tube 1.
Add PEI to tube 2.
Pipette the PEI suspension from tube 2 dropwise to tube 1 and mix by tipping the tube.
Let stand for 15 min at 20°C–24°C.
Add the transfection mix dropwise to the HEK cells across the 10 cm dish.
Slightly rotate the dishes to mix the medium and transfection mix.
Put the dishes back into the incubator.
Prepare fresh lysis buffer with protease and phosphatase inhibitors as described above.
Cool down the lysis buffer and PBS on ice.
Cool down cell lifters and 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes in the cold room.
Cool down the refrigerated table top centrifuge to 4°C.
Prepare a 1 mL pipette and pipette tips in the cold room.
Cool down an aluminum cooling block for 2 mL tubes in an ice bucket in the cold room.
Check the GFP expression in a fluorescence microscope that fits plastic cell culture dishes and is equipped with filters for GFP at 12–15 h after transfection.
Transfer the cell culture dishes to the cold room.
Aspirate the medium from the cell culture dishes.
Wash cells once with 5 mL ice-cold PBS.
Aspirate the PBS and remove any remaining liquid with a pipette.
Detach cells with a cold cell lifter and collect in one spot of the dish.
Add 500 μL of PBS to the collected cells and transfer into a 2 mL tube on ice.
Spin down the cells at 4°C at 400 × g for one minute.
Aspirate the supernatant from the spun-down cells.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of ice-cold lysis buffer.
Adjust the centrifugation speed based on cell requirements.
Disrupt cells with a probe-type sonicator for 10 seconds at 20% amplitude in the cold room.
Rotate tubes containing lysed cells in the cold room for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge cell lysate in a tabletop centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 minutes to remove debris.
Collect supernatants in fresh ice-cold 1 ml microcentrifuge tubes.
Discard pellets after centrifugation.
Collect 50 μL of cell lysate in an ice-cold 1.5 mL tube.
Store the collected sample at 4°C in the refrigerator.
Determine the protein concentration using a BCA assay.
Adjust samples to have equal amounts and concentrations of lysate based on protein concentration.
Probe the expression of housekeeping proteins by immunoblotting.
Add 2 μL of GFP antibody (mouse monoclonal, Roche) to the remaining 950 μL cell lysate.
Thoroughly mix and resuspend the protein-G agarose stock solution to get a homogenous slurry.
Incubate cell lysates with protein-G agarose rotating for 30 min at 4°C in the absence of antibody to reduce non-specific binding.
Spin down the beads at 10 × g, collect the supernatant, and process as described above.
Cut 2 mm from a 1 mL pipette tip.
Transfer the corresponding total volume of slurry to a 2 mL tube.
Fill the tube with ice cold lysis buffer.
Mix the contents of the tube.
Spin down the slurry at 10 × g in a refrigerated table top centrifuge at 4°C.
Repeat the wash step two more times to remove the storage solution from the beads.
Resuspend the beads in 100 μL lysis buffer per sample.
Add 100 μL bead suspension per cell lysate sample.
Rotate the samples in the cold room at 4°C for at least 9–12 h.
Cool down the table top centrifuge.
Thaw an aliquot of 6× sample buffer and warm to 37°C to dissolve precipitated detergent.
Add 10% β-mercaptoethanol (BME) to the 6× sample buffer to establish reducing buffer conditions.
Spin the co-IP samples at 10 × g in the table top centrifuge for 1 min at 4°C to pellet the agarose beads.
Collect the supernatant in a separate 1.5 mL tube for potential follow up analyses.
Leave behind around 100–200 μL liquid in the tube to avoid perturbations of the bead pellet.
Remove the entire liquid from the beads via a 20 μL tip placed at the bottom of the tube, using multiple rounds of aspiration if necessary.
Add 1 mL ice-cold lysis buffer to wash the agarose beads.
Flip the tube upside-down to wash the beads.
Spin the tubes at 10 × g for one minute at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the wash step for two more times.
After a total of three wash steps, use a 20 μL pipette to remove the remaining liquid from the beads.
Place the tip at the bottom of the tube and aspirate the liquid until the beads are dry.
Add 40 μL of 6× sample buffer/10% BME to the beads.
Add 10 μL 6× sample buffer/10% BME to the 50 μL lysate samples collected on day 2.
Heat all co-IP and lysate samples at 95°C for 5 min.
Mix samples by tapping the tubes.
Spin down the mixed samples for 30 s at 10 × g at 20°C–24°C in a table top centrifuge.
Elute proteins with 0.1 M glycine pH 2–3 for 1 min.
Spin down samples for 1 min at 10 × g and collect the supernatant.
Neutralize supernatant with 1 M Tris pH 8.5.
Repeat elution 2–3 times, pool the supernatant.
Add sample buffer to pooled supernatant.
Assemble glass plates on gel casting system.
Add tap water to test for potential leaks in glass plates.
Seal corners of the plates with grease if needed.
Remove and drain the water from the space between the plates after the leak test.
Weigh 10 mg of ammonium persulfate (APS) for a small volume of fresh 10% APS stock solution preparation.
Add 100 μL ddH2O to the weighed APS to prepare the APS solution.
Store leftover 10% APS solution at 4°C, but note it is not stable and loses activity over time.
Mix the Acrylamide/Bis solution, Tris, ddH2O, and TEMED in a 15 mL conical tube at room temperature (20°C–24°C).
Quickly add APS to the mixture and start pouring the gels.
With a 1 mL pipette, add separation gel solution between glass plates to a level 5 mm below the reach of the comb.
Overlay the separation gel with 1 mL of isopropanol to smoothen its surface.
Monitor polymerization state of leftover gel in the conical tube; separation gel polymerization may take 5–10 minutes.
Remove isopropanol from the top of the separation gel by inverting the conical tube.
Rinse the surface of the gel once with ddH2O and remove residual water.
Mix solutions for stacking gel in a 15 mL conical tube in the same order as for the separation gel, adding APS just before casting.
Add the stacking gel solution on top of the separation gel and fill to the top of the glass plates.
Slowly place the comb for either 10 or 15 wells into the gel.
Monitor polymerization status of leftover gel solution in the conical tube.
Once the leftover gel is polymerized, assemble the electrophoresis unit and place it in the buffer tank.
Remove the comb and add running buffer to the top of the chamber.
Flush the wells with a 20 μL pipette using running buffer to remove unpolymerized gel solution.
Let the electrophoresis chamber stand for a couple minutes and check for leaks.
Reassemble the unit or refill with running buffer if needed.
Fill the unit with running buffer until the marks are covered.
Remove air bubbles at the bottom end of the gel with a pipette.
Load the molecular weight standard according to the instructions on the datasheet.
Store leftover samples at −20°C in case some of the immunoblots need to be repeated or additional proteins need to be probed.
Connect the electrophoresis unit to the power supply.
Run the gel at constant 100 V for 90 min and regularly check the fill level of the electrophoresis chamber and the progress of the samples.
Refill the unit with running buffer if necessary.
Prepare 2 L (per 2 gels) of ice cold 1× transfer buffer with 10% ethanol.
Cut the PVDF membrane to cover the gel region of interest and add 5 mm extra membrane.
Cut the Whatman papers to extend 1 cm beyond the gel.
Disassemble the electrophoresis unit and remove one glass plate from the gel.
Use a razor blade to cut away the stacking gel.
Add 1 L of transfer buffer to the transfer unit.
Add 1 L of transfer buffer to a square plastic casserole dish (25 × 25 × 7 cm).
Use enough buffer to submerge all components of the immunoblot sandwich.
Label the PVDF membrane with a pencil (e.g., with date and experiment ID).
Add 10 mL methanol to a small plastic container.
Soak the PVDF membrane in methanol for 2 minutes.
Assemble the immunoblot sandwich in the casserole dish with the white or clear side of the blotting cassette facing down.
Place one sponge and two Whatman papers on the blotting cassette.
Position the wetted PVDF membrane on top of the Whatman papers.
Remove the gel from the glass plate.
Place the gel on top of the PVDF membrane.
Arrange the gel, membrane, and Whatman papers to remove bubbles.
Add two more Whatman papers and another sponge on top of the stack.
Close the cassette with the black lid while keeping the sandwich submerged in transfer buffer.
Place the immunoblot sandwich in the transfer unit with the latch facing up and the black lid facing the black side of the unit.
Move the transfer unit to a cold room and place it in a plastic tray.
Fill the transfer unit to the top with transfer buffer.
Add the lid to the transfer unit.
Place extra weight on the lid to prevent connectivity issues (e.g., use a bottle with leftover buffer).
Connect the transfer unit to the power supply.
Run the transfer at a constant current of 400 mA for 1 hour at 4°C.
Monitor for gas bubbles emerging on the outside of the electrophoresis unit as an indicator of transfer activity.
Prepare 50 mL of 10% dry milk in TBST and pour the solution into a small plastic container.
Once the transfer is completed, take out the transfer cassette and blotting sandwich.
Recover the PVDF membrane and place it in the milk solution.
Block the PVDF membrane for 20 min at 20°C–24°C on a shaker.
Rinse the transfer unit with deionized water.
Rinse the sandwich cassette with deionized water.
Rinse the sponges with deionized water.
Soak the sponges in methanol to remove residual protein.
Rinse the sponges with deionized water after soaking.
Let the sponges dry.
Discard the methanol following hazardous waste protocols.
Prepare primary antibody incubation solutions according to the datasheet instructions.
Use 5% BSA in TBST or 5% dry milk in TBST for small plastic containers.
Dilute the antibody as per prior optimization and instructions.
Incubate PVDF membranes with primary antibody on a shaker at 4°C for 9–12 hours.
Get the membranes from the cold room and collect the primary antibody solution in a 15 mL conical tube.
Label the tube and store at −20°C for reuse.
Add 25 mL TBST to rinse the membrane, and discard the solution.
Repeat for a total of three rinse steps.
Wash the membrane in TBST on the shaker for 20 min at 20°C–24°C.
Repeat the rinse and wash cycle for a total of three times.
Prepare the secondary horseradish peroxidase (HRP) coupled antibodies diluted 1:5000 in a 5% milk/TBST solution.
Incubate the membrane with the HRP-coupled antibodies for 1 h shaking at 20°C–24°C.
Rinse and wash the membrane as described above.
Do three cycles of rinsing and washing the membrane.
Prepare fresh ECL solution.
Incubate the membrane in 10 mL ECL solution for 30-60 seconds at 20°C–24°C.
Drain the membrane and move to a fresh plastic container.
Place the membrane in the blot imaging station.
Adjust the position of the membrane.
Start the image acquisition process.
Record images until the chemiluminescence signal is clearly visible.
Acquire an image of the molecular weight standard on the immunoblot membrane at the end of the imaging series.
Extract images in 16-bit TIF format for densitometry and quantification.
Open Image Studio Light.
Open the image of interest in 16-bit TIF format.
Copy the resulting background subtracted intensity values into a spreadsheet.
Set negative intensity values to zero in the spread sheet.
Record intensity values from co-IP of 14-3-3ε in specific cells (e.g., D4-D6).
Record intensity values of protein bands from co-IP immunoblot for SH3BP4-GFP in designated cells (e.g., D10-D12).
Normalize the signal of prey proteins with the signal from the GFP-tagged bait protein.
Divide the intensity of the co-IP of 14-3-3ε by the intensity of the co-IP of SH3BP4-GFP.
Use the intensity of the control sample to normalize samples with perturbations.
Consider the second sample with the co-IP of SH3BP4-GFP wt in the absence of Akt1-wt-HA overexpression as the control.
Set the normalized value for the control sample to one.
Divide the intensity values of other samples by the intensity value of the control.
Combine normalized values from 3-5 experiments in a spreadsheet.
Calculate arithmetic mean values for combined data.
Use statistical software to calculate mean, error bars, and statistical significance.
Plot the calculated data.
Process immunoblot images to assemble the figure panel.
Open the TIF image in ImageJ/Fiji or your image processing software of choice.
Scale the image intensity.
Crop the region of interest.
Save the processed image in a format compatible with your figure assembly software (e.g., Illustrator, PowerPoint, etc.).
Assemble the figure according to journal guidelines.
